headline: South Asia: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media.
- Western Russia: One killed and 37 injured in Russian attacks on Kherson in a single day.
- Persian Gulf Region: Russian strikes kill civilians, injure dozens across Ukraine.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
- Military Times, 23 hours ago: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
The Army's 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated as the service reshapes its PSYOP and information warfare forces to counter global adversaries.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
A 19-year-old man has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with last Friday’s deadly attack on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, which claimed the lives of two women and a one-year-old boy. The accused, Dante Davis, who has addresses on Spanish Town Road and Kidd Lane in Kingston 13, is also facing charges of conspiracy to commit murder, arson, conspiracy to commit arson, possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and using a firearm to commit a felony.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: One killed and 37 injured in Russian attacks on Kherson in a single day.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: One killed and 37 injured in Russian attacks on Kherson in a single day.
Russian forces launched airstrikes, artillery bombardments and drone attacks on Kherson Oblast on 17 October, leaving one person dead and 40 others injured, including 37 in the city of Kherson.
- Ukrainska Pravda, Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: He was found under rubble by colleagues: Ukrainian emergency worker killed in Russian strike on Donetsk Oblast.
Anatolii Hopka, a 41-year-old rescuer with the State Emergency Service of Ukraine, has been killed in a Russian airstrike on a residential building in Sloviansk.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russians attack Zaporizhstal for fifth time, firing six ballistic missiles – photo.
Russia has attacked the Zaporizhstal steelworks for the fifth time, firing six ballistic missiles at its energy, logistics and production facilities.
- Ukrainska Pravda, South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: Zelenskyy on Trump's decision: Diesel Deal is first step, lifting of Russia sanctions will continue.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Russia sanctions relief and restrictions on Ukraine's ability to respond to Russian attacks would not stop Vladimir Putin and could instead embolden him to continue the war.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Wer führt in Zukunft die SPD? Mit Rasmus Buchsteiner.
- Politico Europe, 9 hours ago: Wer führt in Zukunft die SPD? Mit Rasmus Buchsteiner.
Es war eine Chaoswoche für den Kanzler Friedrich Merz. Das Rentenpaket entwickelt sich zur weiteren Zerreißprobe für die Koalition. Der neue Arbeitsminister Alexander Schweitzer macht es für den Kanzler nicht einfacher. Warum der SPD-Pragmatiker plötzlich auf Konfrontation geht und wie diese Machtkämpfe die Regierungsarbeit lähmen, steht im Zentrum der Analyse. Gleichzeitig brodelt es an der […]

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Russian strikes kill civilians, injure dozens across Ukraine.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: Russian strikes kill civilians, injure dozens across Ukraine.
At least eight people have been killed and nearly 60 injured in the latest wave of Russian strikes across Ukraine.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Israel must treat the media war as seriously as Iran’s nuclear threat, Gil Hoffman says.
MEDIA AFFAIRS: Gil Hoffman talks to the ‘Post’ about his new book 'The Blood Libel Machine' and Israel’s war for global public opinion.
- Jerusalem Post, one day ago: IDF kills Hamas Nukhba commander in Gaza who infiltrated Re'im base on October 7.
Since the October 7 attacks, the terrorist continued his involvement in planning terror attacks against Israeli soldiers and civilians, the military noted.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: WATCH: Masked settlers allegedly attack European diplomats, Palestinians in West Bank.
Masked settlers allegedly attacked Palestinian olive harvesters near Taybeh, damaging a Belgian diplomatic vehicle. Police have opened an investigation.
Africa - bottom line: Iran denies being behind Houthi attacks as Aden airport hit.
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Iran denies being behind Houthi attacks as Aden airport hit.
Iran has denied any involvement in an escalation of attacks by Houthi rebels on Saudi targets. The international airport in Yemen’s interim capital Aden was struck by two missiles late on Friday, the second such incident in less than two weeks.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 23 hours ago: Uganda: MP Calls for Probe Into Recruitment of Ugandans to Fight for Russia.
[Nile Post] Rukiga County MP Patrick Katabaazi has asked the government to investigate reports that Ugandan youths are being recruited through deceptive job offers and deployed to fight for Russia in the war against Ukraine.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Media Statement - Defence Committee Calls for Urgent Action to Reverse SANDF Decline.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Media Statement - Defence Committee Calls for Urgent Action to Reverse SANDF Decline.
[Parliament of South Africa] The Portfolio Committee on Defence and Military Veterans has called for urgent intervention to reverse the decline of the South African National Defence Force (SANDF), warning that persistent resource shortages, financial pressures and governance weaknesses are undermining the country's defence capability.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Katherine O'regan Receives George Bizos Human Rights Award, Warns of Shift to Authoritarianism.
[Daily Maverick] On 15 October, former Constitutional Court Justice Katherine O'Regan received the George Bizos Human Rights Award, reflecting on the project of democracy and urging resistance to rising authoritarianism.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: Zimbabwe: Poverty, Injustice Threaten Lasting Peace in Zimbabwe - ZPP.
[263Chat] The Zimbabwe Peace Project (ZPP) has called for greater investment in justice, human rights and inclusive institutions warning that poverty, inequality and weak access to justice continue to threaten lasting peace in Zimbabwe.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media.
Security forces have responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Upper Kurram, state broadcaster PTV News reported on Saturday. PTV News and state-run Associated Press of Pakistan (APP), which cited security sources, said the Afghan Taliban forces opened fire to “facilitate terrorists” along the border in Taldah sector of Upper Kurram. The army responded using heavy weapons, destroying several Afghan Taliban posts and forcing their personnel to flee from there, PTV News reported.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Iran backs 'political process' to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran supports a “political process” to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi rebels. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a major attack last week. “We support an inclusive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue,” Araghchi said in a speech at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump.
President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine. The move came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders to keep financing Kyiv’s fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, insisting he was standing up for his country as Trump’s support slumped.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: North Korea says tested AI-assisted torpedo system.
North Korea has tested a “new-type” precision-guided torpedo system that uses artificial intelligence for target detection and guidance, state media reported Saturday, as the nuclear-armed country steps up weapons testing. The announcement came days after Pyongyang said it had test-fired two types of cruise missiles from a submarine after weeks of friction with Seoul over a landmine explosion along their border.

- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: How Taiwan’s new AI satellite system aims to speed up early warning against PLA moves.
Taiwan will acquire an AI-powered satellite imagery system capable of rapidly identifying People’s Liberation Army ships, aircraft and missile launchers, as it seeks to boost early-warning capabilities in the face of growing military pressure from Beijing. A teacher threw her phone at the teenage gunman who killed four people at an Oregon junior school, then tackled and fought with him – probably saving lives before he was shot by a father who followed him into the building, police said Friday. Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz called the teacher’s actions “heroic” during a news conference and said she was not injured. He identified the attacker as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II and said all of the victims were shot in the same classroom. Authorities...
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Albanian police fire rubber bullets as student protesters call for PM to quit.
Police in Albania fired what appeared to be rubber bullets at protesters on Saturday, the fifth day of mass student protests demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama step down. Reuters video footage showed police firing a shotgun towards crowds outside the education ministry during clashes with protesters. Reuters reporters found rubber pellets on the ground and pellets hit two Reuters journalists ‌and several protesters, leaving round marks. ‘rewards’ Putin: Zelenskiy.
India - bottom line: Man killed, four injured in suspected militant attack on Kuki village in Manipur.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Man killed, four injured in suspected militant attack on Kuki village in Manipur.
A tragic incident unfolded in Chassad village, Manipur, where a militant attack led to the death of one man and injuries to four others. Gunfire erupted between the militants and a local armed faction, with the violence persisting into the evening. Emergency services promptly transported the injured to a hospital, but sadly, one victim did not survive.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 14 hours ago: 'I love you' on clothes & a chilling note: What preceded Gurgaon techie couple's deaths.
An IT professional, Mohammad Aslam, and his wife, Farhana, were discovered dead in their Gurgaon apartment. Aslam sent an alarming email to his employer before the incident, indicating a distressing situation. Police suspect that Aslam may have killed his wife before taking his own life. Relatives claim that Aslam had been struggling with depression for about 18 months prior to the tragedy.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Why Trump's plan to unleash 'Mother Of All Bombs' may fall flat in Iran.
Military discussions are considering the use of the MOAB against Iran's nuclear facilities and military targets. However, the effectiveness of the MOAB is limited against deeply buried sites protected by reinforced concrete. Analysts highlight that the GBU-57 penetrator is better suited for such underground facilities, which require specialized weapons for effective targeting. While the MOAB has a strong psychological impact, its military utility against hardened targets is questionable.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: "Will Be Crushed Under Weight Of Power": Pak Opposition Leader Warns Military.
Addressing a public gathering in Punjab's Multan district on Friday, Rehman said Pakistan could function effectively only when the military, bureaucracy and elected institutions operated within their respective constitutional domains.

- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: Starlink speed restrictions ground interceptors as Russian strikes batter Ukraine.
Ukraine is grappling with Starlink restrictions vital to operating its interceptors as Trump pauses some Russian sanctions.

South-eastern Victoria has been slightly shaken by an earthquake aftershock, three weeks after an overnight tremor woke thousands.
